first.rationale: Triage logic: verify the beliefs that are both decision-critical this week and weakest against the stated objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue). memory_73 (promotional pricing) is the most consequential because the competitor's entry pricing makes it the obvious reflex, and its recorded support is acquisition and revenue lift only — it says nothing about margin persistence, retention, or whether the acquired accounts stayed qualified after the discount lapsed. Discount-led growth is the classic case where a headline win masks value dilution downstream, so committing the single slot to it on unverified proxy evidence is the largest exposure. memory_91 is the second pull because activation is the biggest decline (-6% QoQ) and it is the memory I currently intend to act on; its support is 'week-one engagement' and 'first meaningful action' — both early proxies that may not translate into retained, qualified revenue. Verifying my own intended action's evidence is the point of the invariant, not verifying the alternatives I have already ruled out. I did not spend budget on memory_57 (referral) because it already records the long-horizon check I care about — qualified revenue with no measurable retention harm — but it targets established customers and does not address the activation/onboarding decline driving this quarter. memory_44 (enterprise) is well-scoped to pipeline quality but off-target for an SMB-pressure quarter. memory_31 and memory_86 both point at onboarding and are mutually corroborating, so the marginal value of pulling one is lower; onboarding remains my fallback if memory_91's record turns out to be engagement-only with no durable follow-through. Intended action: activation_messaging at standard experiment scale, instrumented past the proxy — measure 30/90-day retention and revenue quality, not just week-one engagement, and treat the inherited lift as directional rather than established. If the archive shows memory_91 rested purely on same-week engagement counts, I will downgrade to a guarded test or shift the slot to simplify_onboarding, which has two independent supporting records. If memory_73's record shows durable post-discount retention, promotional pricing becomes viable later, but it would not be my first slot regardless: it is the least reversible move and the hardest to unwind once customers anchor on the discounted price.

final.rationale:
Both pulls paid off, in opposite directions. memory_73 is now actively disconfirmed for this objective: exp_73 shows signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% but 30-day retention -12%, with an explicit source-record instruction not to generalize targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The inherited summary had compressed a cautionary result into an endorsement by keeping the headline numbers and dropping the renewal-cycle failure. Promotional_pricing is therefore off the table this week despite being the most intuitive answer to competitor entry pricing — it would buy acquisition against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and it is the least reversible move once customers anchor on a discounted price. I am flagging that memory_73 should be rewritten in durable memory with its retention finding attached, or the next agent inherits the same trap.

memory_91 came back confirmed and, importantly, confirmed on the axis I was worried about: activation +6% with 30-day retention +1%. My concern was that it rested on week-one engagement as a proxy; the record carries the retention follow-through, so the lift is not a pull-forward of engagement that decays. Activation is also the largest current decline at -6% QoQ, and exp_91's recorded activation effect is +6% — directly matched to the gap, on the metric that moved.

Committing the slot to activation_messaging at standard experiment scale. Standard rather than broad because a single confirmed record at one point in time does not establish that the effect holds under current conditions — competitor pressure changes the mix of accounts arriving, and the original cohort may not resemble today's. Standard rather than small-guarded because the evidence is verified rather than speculative and a underpowered test wastes a non-carrying slot. I will instrument past the proxy again: 30 and 90-day retention and revenue quality, not just week-one engagement, so the next agent inherits an outcome record rather than another headline.

simplify_onboarding remains the fallback and is genuinely close — onboarding completion is down 4% and memory_31 and memory_86 corroborate each other independently. I chose activation because the decline is larger and its supporting record is now verified end-to-end, whereas the onboarding pair remains unverified and could contain the same summary-drift failure that memory_73 did. Residual uncertainty: neither onboarding memory has been checked against retention, and the competitor pricing pressure is a real revenue threat that activation messaging does not directly answer — it addresses the funnel we control rather than the price comparison we do not.
